chunks: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Aziz al-Samarqandi, the Jurist at Balkh, said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Zahid al-Samarqandi, with his own chain, raised it to al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), that a man asked him, saying: 'Verily, the foundation of religion is Divine Unity and Divine Justice, and His Knowledge is vast, and a wise man cannot do without it. So mention what makes it easy to grasp and suitable for memorization.' He (peace be upon him) answered: 'As for Divine Unity, it is that you do not attribute to your Lord what is permissible for you [to have], and as for Divine Justice, it is that you do not attribute to your Creator what you do not have power over.'
ai.seo_question: What are the definitions of Divine Unity and Divine Justice according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this concise definition from *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) anchors the theological pillars of Tawhid and Adl in the concept of anthropomorphism, defining Unity as avoiding the attribution of human limitations to God and Justice as excluding human imperfections from His essence. This formulation serves as a foundational principle in Shia kalām, emphasizing that divine attributes must be understood through negation of creaturely defects rather than positive analogy. It reflects the scholarly tradition of distinguishing between God's essential attributes and His actions, ensuring that justice is intrinsic to His nature rather than an external imposition.
